To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the current approach to social project management is marked by a positivist and linear bias; 2. in more complex projects this approach has shown limitations, especially in relation to collective actions aimed at social change; 3. the blind watchmaker approach, based on a systemic and constructivist logic, has proven to be more adequate for the management of social projects with a focus on collective actions.
the blind watchmaker approach to social project management, which is based on a causal logic and positivist bias, is not effective in the management of collective actions aimed at social change.
